fields.title: Polka: fast screen, unhappy people
fields.summary: The server serves the screen in 380 ms, but app store reviews say it "lags" in every sixth review.
fields.decisionPrompt: Where do we start? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are the Polka product manager. According to reports, the main screen is served by the server in 380 ms at p95—double the target. Meanwhile, drop-off before the main screen loads is 8%, and "laggy" appears in every sixth app store review.
fields.brief/objective: Understand who is experiencing slowness and start fixing it without wasting a week on guesswork.
fields.brief/constraints: No client-side metrics exist at all; implementing them takes a week.
fields.brief/task: Decide where to start and what to measure.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Server percentiles tell you nothing about the user
fields.learnTakeaway/body: 380 ms on the server and 6.8 seconds for a person on an old phone are the same system. As long as measurements stop at the server boundary, you optimize your own piece and miss the rest. Implement client metrics—but do not turn a week of waiting into a week of inactivity: working on perceived performance takes days and does not prevent measurement.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: p50 = 190 ms, p95 = 380 ms, p99 = 640 ms. Stable.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: No client metrics. Implementation takes a week.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: Flagship, Wi-Fi: 0.9 s to interactivity. 4-year-old device, 4G: 3.4 s. 4-year-old device, weak signal: 6.8 s.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Devices older than 4 years — 18%. Sessions with weak signal — 22%. Intersection — about 4%.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Implement client metrics, then decide. One week.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: a clear picture emerges. A week without improvements despite a known problem. Manual measurements already show a 7x gap—part of the solution is obvious even without metrics.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Lighten response and images. Two weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: attacks the largest known cause — 2.1 MB of images. Without metrics, it is unknown how much it helps and for whom. Risk of not measuring the result.
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Skeleton screen and rendering order. Four days.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: the fastest option. Does not speed up, improves perception and should reduce drop-off. Does not solve the 6.8 seconds in the difficult segment.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Metrics and perception in parallel, then lighten
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Metrics and perception in parallel, then lighten. One week for two streams, then two weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: after a week, you have both a clear picture and the first improvement. Then lightening with the ability to measure the effect. Three weeks total.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not distinguish between server and client time
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Reads the median instead of the segment distribution
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not see perceived performance as a separate lever
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Average and p95 are read as describing all users
